items.title: Priya applied to 312 jobs and got three interviews
items.summary: Priya applied to 312 jobs and got three interviews. Mass applying with AI doesn't work. The fix is smaller: find the 15 roles where you're the obvious choice. Write one sentence: the kind of company, the kind of role, and the one skill you're best at. Hers was Senior PM roles at Series B or C B2B SaaS companies, where she can use her enterprise workflow expertise. Then you only apply where that sentence is true. Lower volume, higher success rate. Source: my Unicorn Candidate-Market Fit newsletter, Oct 31 2025. #shorts #pmjobs

items.title: How To Build The Future: Paul Graham & Amjad Masad
items.summary: Replit was building toward the AI coding era years before it had a name. In 2024, the company shipped an agent that could take a request in plain English, work through errors, provision its own infrastructure, and keep going until the software actually worked. The model companies even reached out to ask how Replit had pulled it off. Co-founder and CEO Amjad Masad had been thinking about making programming radically more accessible since 2008, and Replit’s original pitch deck predicted AI-generated code before the Transformer paper was published. Today, that same technology is moving into banks, manufacturers, and other large companies, where Amjad says teams are replacing software projects once scoped at $10 million with $250,000 of Replit. On How to Build the Future, Paul Graham sits down with Amjad to talk about why Replit was so well positioned when coding agents arrived, what comes after vibe coding, and his bigger vision for the “self-driving company,” where AI agents increasingly build and operate the software a company needs. items.title: Do you understand what happened in AI security in the last seven days?
items.summary: Do you understand what happened in AI security in the last seven days? One hacker pointed AI agents at more than 1,200 sites and got into more than 100 companies, including Deere and Cummins. The whole run cost about $5,000, and the average break-in took 23 hours. Microsoft says a Chinese-aligned group used agentic AI against ConnectWise customers. More than 2,250 Microsoft 365 tenants were targeted and 327 accounts were compromised. LiteLLM, an AI tool with over 20 million downloads a week, shipped a version that steals credentials. It was live for about two hours. Anthropic's IPO filing says four of its models gained unauthorized access to real third-party systems. Sources are in the first comment. Sources: Norforge via The Hacker News (Oct 20), Microsoft Security blog (Oct 21), LiteLLM incident post (Oct 21), Anthropic Form S-1 (Oct 26). #shorts #aisecurity

items.title: Kinh tế tăng trưởng, ai hưởng lợi đầu tiên?
